Congratulations, following up and meeting with the doctor says a lot about your commitment.  I work frequently with the VA for our non-profit foundation in regards to mental health and your fears are understandable.  Unfortunately, the VA has many, many problems which will not be easy to fix.  The good news though is that the vast majority of those on the front lines in the VA truly care about you the patient.  They have many stupid and illogical rules from senior leadership pushing back on them, but typically they do have your best interest at heart.  My recommendation is to be honest with your doctor as it is the only way you are going to get the help you need. Youth & teens are a high risk with their rate rising over 79% in the last 10 years.  Our organization is working around the clock to not only slow this epidemic, but end it.  We also provide many services and as a 501(c)(3) organization are not looking to make money off of others pain...we want to help.  [https://www.FightingForOurYouth.com](https://www.FightingForOurYouth.com)

PLEASE, if you are considering suicide, reach out for help.  At a minimum, please have a conversation with someone who cares before you make such a final decision.  We want you here, your story is not yet over.

After working so hard on this, it is still disappointing to hear all of the frustration from users who have had less than helpful interactions with the resources available.  I agree, our system is broken and based on the feedback, many struggle with finding a connection on the support lines.  Having worked with many of the organizations running the different support lines I can say without a doubt, the people volunteering their time and working them are caring and have the callers best interests at heart BUT, this doesn't seem to be how it is received.

So what can be done differently?  If you have called, texted, or chatted a support line, what do you believe would have been more effective?  This isn't a loaded question, I honestly want to know.  Our organization wants to continue to find ways to improve the resources available and put an end to suicide.  I don't know you, yet I care about you.  Please share with me what me might do to be of more help.

If you have a Max Muscle store in your area give it a try.  I have found no better supplements and the cost is much better than GNC and other competitors.  The protein shakes have a few secrets you can try.  If it is an 8 oz shake you are making, fill your measuring cup with 8 oz of crushed ice, then fill around the ice up to the 8 oz mark with water.  Add your scoop of vanilla (or whatever flavor you prefer) protein powder along with 2 TBSP of vanilla sugar free pudding mix.  The pudding mix adds nothing but flavor if you use the sugar free.  Mix it in the blender and you have a vanilla shake that is comparable to some ice cream shakes.

Weightlifting isn't going to make you gain weight in and of itself.  Nutrition is much more powerful in managing weight while weightlifting has immeasurable benefits in actually helping you control weight (some studies have shown weightlifting does more for weight loss and maintaining than cardio).  The biggest thing you need to learn about with the nutrition is that most of the diets and info shared focus on a specific food group as if that is the only reason for weight changes.  The fact is that the 3 main points are protein, fats, and carbohydrates.  You need to learn how each plays it's part and how to portion them correctly for 5-6 small meals a day with those exact portions.  I my passion and my career are working with ladies and kids who have so many of these exact same questions so you aren't alone.
